entries.test: Public audience and retention trends, together with studies of Facebook's engagement incentives, could establish whether those incentives are causing sustained platform decline.
entries.note: In context, 'slowly killing' has a plain reading of causing sustained decline.

entries.test: Representative Facebook content audits and public usage trends for Meta's family of products could test the prevalence of AI engagement bait and the asserted ongoing decline.
entries.note: The proposition turns 'even if' into an unconditional assertion about what the metric represents. AI-generated engagement bait is described as prevalent, not as an antecedent condition.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of Meta AI's interaction and publishing features, alongside studies of interactions with resulting content, could test whether it creates the described additional opportunities for engagement.
entries.note: The claim concerns additional opportunities and reasons to interact, without specifying a numerical increase in engagement.
This is an overall judgment of the features' worth and intrusiveness, without a specified empirical standard.
The spending-guidance figures are independently checkable in Meta's disclosures. They cannot settle the central judgment that the spending is senseless.
The metaverse spending and hardware purchases are separately checkable. 'Seems to be intent' makes the comparable AI spending commitment a hedged inference.

entries.test: Public usage records and an eventual Facebook shutdown or cessation as an operating social network, together with Instagram's trajectory if Meta encounters difficulties, would test the predicted outcomes.
entries.note: The main Facebook prediction is firm and undated; 'I believe' introduces an asserted forecast. The Instagram prediction has an explicit condition.
